claims.text: The starting alloy is equiatomic Hf-Zr-Mo-Cu-Ni, with approximately 20 at.% of each element.
Arc melting produces this composition as a homogeneous solid solution.
The as-cast starting alloy is fully chemically disordered.
The proposed intervention is annealing at approximately 800 °C under high vacuum for 1 hour followed by rapid quenching.
The specified annealing and quenching treatment will induce and freeze in nanoscale chemical ordering.
Annealing will produce nanoscale chemically ordered clusters within an otherwise disordered matrix.
Short-range chemical order modifies the local bonding environment.
Short-range chemical order modifies the alloy's electronic structure and density of states at the Fermi level.
The ordering-induced changes in bonding and electronic structure alter electron-phonon coupling strength.
Changes in electron-phonon coupling and Fermi-level density of states govern the superconducting transition temperature.
Annealed samples will have a higher superconducting transition temperature than as-cast samples.
Annealed samples will have a narrower superconducting transition than as-cast samples.
Changes in transition temperature and transition width will correlate with the presence and degree of local chemical ordering.
The proposed mechanism applies only when annealing induces nanoscale ordering without full phase separation or secondary-phase formation.
The annealed material remains a solid solution rather than transforming into a multiphase material.

contradictions.description: The annealed and as-cast samples cannot literally be under identical processing conditions because annealing and quenching are the intervention. The comparison is coherent only if 'identical' means identical except for that intervention.
